messages.author: 6ba398eb62cb3b97
messages.subject: Non-fatal error message
parts:
Dear Stan-Developers,

Thank you very much for Stan - I started a couple of days ago as I was stuck with my model in JAGS. I used some mock data to check my code and I found that it mostly works when I run:

fit.qre <- stan(file = 'QreThreePlayer.stan', data = c("N", "Nmis1", "Nmis2", "Y1", "Y2", "Y3", "x11", "x12", "x14", "x22", "x24", "x34", "x22mis1", "x24mis1", "x34mis1", "x34mis2"), iter = 300, chains = 4)

But sometimes I get this error message:

Warning (non-fatal rejection): Error in function stan::prob::normal_log<N4stan5agrad3varE>(N4stan5agrad3varE): Random variate y is nan:0, but must not be nan!

This warning occurs for an entire chain and hence I end up with estimates of usually only 2 out of the 4 chains. I was now able to reproduce an error in the very first run (creating "fit.qre"). Can you explain what this error indicates? I have right now no idea how to fix this issue. I am attaching the model file (QreThreePlayer.stan) and some R code (showerror.R) setting up data and running the models.

Best,

Lucas

messages.author: ba46e0c634632e6f
messages.subject: Re: Non-fatal error message
parts: I'm sure a developer will have a possible fix, but I resolved a similar issue with a logistic regression by changing bernoulli(inv_logit()) to bernoulli_logit(). Looks to me like you're dong some sort of probit, but I don't know what sort of solution you'd need for that.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non-fatal error message
parts:
Switching to using bernoulli_logit() is definitely a good idea and may
resolve this issue. Also, you are declaring a lot of arrays which
aren't needed and vectorization would make your model run much faster.
E.G.,

for (n in 1:Nmis2){
real p3lat2[Nmis2];
p3lat2[n] <- alpha34 + beta34*x34mis2[n];
Y3[n] ~ bernoulli(Phi(p3lat2[n]));
}

Can just be

for (n in 1:Nmis2){
Y3[n] ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha34 + beta34*x34mis2[n]);
}


or, with vectorization,

Y3 ~ bernoulli_logit(alpha34 + beta34*x34mis2);


Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Non-fatal error message
parts:
On Sun, Sep 23, 2012 at 12:44 PM, Lucas Leemann <llee...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi Marcus and Ryan,
>
> Thanks a lot for the hints how to speed up - it is indeed not nicely coded as I was trying to debug things.
>
> What is it exactly that makes the bernoulli_logit(*) so much better than bernoulli(Phi(*))?

The short version is that Phi() can be poorly (numerically) behaved on
its own. When combined with the bernoulli function things can be done
a bit more intelligently, saving both computation and making things
more accurate.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: bernoulli_logit(x) vs. bernoulli(logit(x)) vs. bernoulli(Phi(x))
parts:
The bernoulli_logit(x) is the same as bernoulli(logit(x)),
but is better behaved numerically.

Can we build a bernoulli_inv_Phi() that would be better
behaved numerically than bernoulli(Phi(x))? I'm thinking,
for instance, we might be able to lean on erfc in the
bernoulli, given that we need to compute (1 - Phi(x)) in
the outcome y=0 case.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] bernoulli_logit(x) vs. bernoulli(logit(x)) vs. bernoulli(Phi(x))
parts:
The distributions that allow vectorization
have "reals" as their variable types.

For regular functions, they'll be listed
with argument type real[].

Neither the inv_logit function nor the
bernoulli or bernoulli_logit were vectorized
in 1.0.1, but both bernoulli and bernoulli_logit
will be in 1.0.2. We'll eventually get around to
vectorizing all the unary functions, too.

The 1.0.2 manual will also have a hotlinked index
of functions and signatures that should simplify
looking this info up.

- Bob
